The author documents 'parallel, pwsh, osascript, vim -c' as a residual, but the class is much wider and each case was DENIED before this package.

In h_env treat any NAME=... word (literal or not) as an assignment. Walk command-valued git settings and env vars (diff.external, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, core.pager/GIT_PAGER, core.sshCommand/GIT_SSH_COMMAND, core.fsmonitor, credential.helper '!', filter.*, mergetool/difftool *.cmd, difftool -x/--extcmd, grep -O, bisect run, submodule foreach) as code with run_code, or mark them unseen when not literal. Anchor _ENV_GENERATOR on the whole substitution (the nested script must be exactly one allowlisted command with literal arguments, nothing chained, piped or concatenated), drop 'asdf exec' and path-qualified names. Make xargs with unknown input and a literal git/gh program a guess over git/gh (possible commit/push/pr), non-literal trap code and interpreter -c/-e code unseen, add /dev/fd/N and /proc/self/fd/N to the stdin names, treat any write to a path ending in /config under a dynamic git dir (or any dynamic write before a git alias lookup) as config_unknown, and mirror config_unknown for gh (GH_CONFIG_DIR, writes to gh/config.yml, gh extension install).

issues.location: hooks/lib/tool-input/shell_analysis.py:1794-1797 (tick: deadline checked every 64 steps only), 1874-1891 (expand_atoms: unbounded value sizes), 1065 (_SUBSCRIPT_EXEC quadratic), 2468-2474 (h_shell_state applies it to every literal argument), 60-63 (MAX_INPUT_CHARS 2 MiB vs three analyses per dev-cycle-check call); docs/ENFORCEMENT.md:49 ('never a timeout')
issues.problem: The budgets do not bound real work, so the agent can still push completion-audit and dev-cycle-check past their 15 s hook timeout (host treats it as non-blocking, so the command runs). (a) Per-step cost is unbounded: variable values are concatenated without a size cap and every step runs regexes over them, while the wall clock is only checked every 64 steps; 25 doublings of a 4-byte value take 15+ s even inside 'if false' (bash runs it in 17 ms). (b) _SUBSCRIPT_EXEC (new in a985913) backtracks quadratically on '[' runs and is applied to each literal argument of export/declare/read/unset; one regex call cannot be interrupted by the step budget. (c) dev-cycle-check starts the analyzer three times per Bash call (write paths, invoked script, read-only), each allowed ~3 s of parsing plus 4 s of walking, so a 1 MB command (half of MAX_INPUT_CHARS) times out. The docstring claim 'none can raise or hang a hook' and ENFORCEMENT.md 'never a timeout' are false.

issues.suggested_fix: Bound the cost of each step, not only the number of steps: cap stored variable/feed values (e.g. 64 KiB; larger values become Dyn and, if later executed, unseen), check the deadline on every tick (time.monotonic is cheap) and inside expansion loops, and make every regex applied to command text linear (_SUBSCRIPT_EXEC as r'\[[^\]$`]*(?:\$\(|`)' or a manual scan; same audit for _GLOB_CHARS '\[.*\]'). Size the budgets for the worst hook: a total analysis budget well under 15 s divided by the number of analyses a hook makes, or a much lower MAX_INPUT_CHARS (honest commands are rarely >100 KB) so that oversized input is unseen at once; until dev-cycle-check adopts sb_tool_input_load, give the accessors a shared per-process budget or cache. Add regression tests that run the doubling, the bracket run and a 1 MB command through completion-audit and dev-cycle-check under 'timeout 15' and assert a deny.

issues.problem: Arithmetic evaluation is modelled for (( )), $(( )), $[ ], let and [[ -eq ]] only. Bash also evaluates array subscripts in parameter expansions (${a[x]}, ${a[x]:-z}), substring offsets/lengths (${x:x}), 'declare -i y=x' / 'local -i' assignments and '[[ -v $x ]]'; with x='a[$(cmd)]' each runs cmd. These forms get tier none and read_only=true, so they hide delivery from completion-audit and source writes from dev-cycle-check (R2-02/R4-04).

issues.problem: The rejection 'Plain git pull, git stash and git checkout -B / switch -C create no commits of the agent's own and are not gated' is not sound. git stash turns the agent's uncommitted work into a commit object, and checkout -B / switch -C / reset to that stash ref move the current branch onto it: the agent's own work lands as commits on the branch without the planning floor. The reset rule only covers a dynamic revision ($(git stash create)), not the literal stash ref. 'git pull . other' is gated but the same local merge spelled './', "$PWD" or '.git' is not.
